messages.author: 98429091c3e0ab77
messages.subject: Offline Installation-Package for Shiny-Server
parts:
Dear Shiny-Team,

would there possibly be an offline installation-Package for Shiny-Server (for beta version as well as for the later enterprise version)? 
In the company our servers have apparently no internet access for security considerations. 

Thank you very much for your replies in advance!

Best regards, 

Yinchong

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Offline Installation-Package for Shiny-Server
parts:
I just added a script to the GitHub repository to let you build an offline installer for the shiny-server package itself. You will still have to install Node.js, R, and the Shiny R package (along with its dependencies) though.

For the Shiny R package, if you have either an Internet-connected server or a virtual machine that has the same OS version installed (including 32 vs. 64 bit) then you could install the Shiny package and copy the entire site library (on Ubuntu, for example, it's /usr/local/lib/R/site-library).

For the Shiny Server package, do this on an Internet-connected machine with git and Node.js installed:

git clone https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server
cd shiny-server
node tools/bundle-offline-installer.js

That will generate a file like "shiny-server-0.2.2.tgz" in the current directory. Copy it to your server, and from the server run this command:

npm install --no-registry -g shiny-server-0.2.2.tgz

Let me know if you have any other problems.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Offline Installation-Package for Shiny-Server
parts: I didn't realize there was another dependency that doesn't get packed: as part of the rebuild process it needs the source files for node itself. Assuming you are running Node 0.8.18 on your Ubuntu box, you should be able to find it at ~/.node-gyp/0.8.18. Copy that directory to the same location in the home directory on the Red Hat box. Once shiny-server is successfully installed you can delete it, I believe.

parts:
I am trying to host a shiny app on a windows machine. I tried to follow the instructions i.e. downloading node.js. Can you provide more detail on getting my windows machine able to host a shiny app. I am just not understanding the instructions.
Sorry but appreciate the assistance.
Nathan
On Thursday, January 17, 2013 9:24:47 AM UTC-8, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:

I just added a script to the GitHub repository to let you build an offline installer for the shiny-server package itself. You will still have to install Node.js, R, and the Shiny R package (along with its dependencies) though.

For the Shiny R package, if you have either an Internet-connected server or a virtual machine that has the same OS version installed (including 32 vs. 64 bit) then you could install the Shiny package and copy the entire site library (on Ubuntu, for example, it's /usr/local/lib/R/site-library).

For the Shiny Server package, do this on an Internet-connected machine with git and Node.js installed:

git clone https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server
cd shiny-server
node tools/bundle-offline-installer.js

That will generate a file like "shiny-server-0.2.2.tgz" in the current directory. Copy it to your server, and from the server run this command:

npm install --no-registry -g shiny-server-0.2.2.tgz

Let me know if you have any other problems.
